pylons_vi: 2 tháp chữ Y ngược, chân kim cương dưới mặt cầu, cao 175,3 m
pylons_en: 2 inverted-Y pylons with diamond feet below the deck, 175.3 m

pylon_custom.description: Inverted Y with a DIAMOND foot. Two straight, heavy legs come down from a long single head, splay outward and pass just outside the deck edges, where a cross-beam carries the deck. Below the deck they converge INWARD to a footing ≈0.55 × the leg spread at the deck, leaving an arched opening under the deck beam. The legs merge ≈40% of the above-deck height (≈56 m); the tapered single head (≈60%) carries a dense fan of stays in two planes.

model3d.notes: Shape read from Commons photos (pylon close-up from the deck; tower under construction 2007, which shows the A-frame legs and the under-deck strut). Height 175.3 m total (mageba), of which ≈135 m above deck. Side-span auxiliary piers at 40 m spacing (2×40 m end spans). Stays fan from the single head to both deck edges. Steel box girder in the main span, concrete in the side spans.

review: Pass 1 claimed A-frame splayed feet — wrong

notes: Pass 2 (2026-11-26): corrected from the client's sunset photo and Commons side views (Anh Khoa 32866753646 / 32907235505): below the deck the legs converge to a narrower footing (diamond), not an A-frame splay. Merge ≈56 m above deck (≈40%, measured on photos 21 and 24: head ≈57–62% of the above-deck height); head ≈79 m. Auxiliary piers at 40 and 80 m from each unit end (2 × 40 m end spans); unit length 930 m, so 850/890 from the start. Steel box main span.
